coverage_notes:
WHAT IS SOLID: The on-field tier is complete and comes from a single contemporaneous source - the Seattle Times' published "Washington Rose Bowl Roster" (Jan 3, 1992, two days after the Rose Bowl that clinched the coaches-poll title), whose "COACHES:" line names exactly ten men: Don James plus nine assistants (Lambright, Gilbertson, Corrigan, Hart, Simon, Slade, Tormey, Wentworth, Woodruff). Nine full-time assistants was the NCAA maximum in that era, so this list is almost certainly the entire on-field staff as of the championship game. Every one of those ten is cited to that line, and eight of them have at least one corroborating source. No one on the list arrived or departed mid-season (Wentworth was hired in March 1991; Gilbertson coached the Rose Bowl and only then left to become Cal's head coach for 1992), so no midseason_note applies to anyone.

CORRECTION TO A COMMON ERROR: Wikipedia's "1991 Washington Huskies football navbox" lists Al Lavan among the 1991 assistant coaches, and Lavan's own Wikipedia article says "Washington (1991-1995)". That is wrong by a year. Lavan does not appear on the January 1992 Seattle Times staff line; Matt Simon was the 1991 running backs coach (Simon's Wikipedia infobox: Washington RB/K 1982-1991), and the 1993 Washington media guide lists "Al Lavan (2nd year)" as cornerbacks coach, i.e. he started in 1992. Lavan is therefore excluded.

TIERS I COULD NOT RECOVER:
1. No 1991 or 1992 media guide exists anywhere I could reach. archive.org holds Washington football media guides for 1989 and 1993-1998 only (identifiers washington-football-YYYY-media-guide-c); there is no 1990, 1991 or 1992 volume. The Wayback Machine's earliest captures postdate 1996, so no contemporaneous athletics-site staff directory exists for fall 1991 / January 1992 - the "school site archived near the title date" step is simply unavailable for a 1991 team. gohuskies.com/sports/football/coaches/1991 returns HTTP 200 but renders the current staff, not 1991.
2. Graduate assistants: only Jeff Mills is documented. NCAA rules then allowed two GAs, so there is very likely a second 1991 GA I could not name. The 1993 media guide's two GAs (Wayne Dickens, Rick Mallory) are each listed in their second year, meaning both started in 1992, so neither fills the 1991 slot.
3. Strength staff: Huegli (head) and Gillespie (assistant, joined 1991) are documented. A third name in the 1993 guide, Stephanie Armitage-Johnson, is listed in her second year (started 1992) and is therefore excluded.
4. Operations/personnel/recruiting: only Dick Baird is documented. The football office staff listed in the 1993 media guide (secretary Peggy Watson, "9th year"; program assistant Connie Bone, "5th year") would by those tenures have been present in 1991, but I found no 1991-dated source for either, and the media-guide text is only available as noisy OCR, so I did not create rows for them. There was no "director of football operations" position on this staff in 1991 - Myles Corrigan became the program's first, in 1994, after his coaching career ended.
5. Medical, equipment, video: not recoverable at the team level. Washington's trainers (head trainer Dennis Sealey and seven assistant trainers), equipment managers (Tony Piro plus five assistants) and film/video staff appear in the 1993 media guide as athletic-department-wide personnel, not as football-team staff, and I found no source assigning any of them to the 1991 football team specifically. No team physician is documented in any accessible source.
6. Analyst and quality-control tiers did not exist in 1991 college football; there are no rows for them, and their absence is real rather than a gap in coverage.

QUOTE MECHANICS: Every quote above was verified as an exact byte-for-byte substring of the raw HTML served at the given URL (verified programmatically). Wikipedia quotes were deliberately kept to link-free fragments because wikilinks become markup in converted page text; for Chris Tormey the only Wikipedia evidence lives in infobox table cells, so his quote is minimal and the Seattle Times line is his real support. The Seattle Times line contains an original typo, "Randy Hart (defensive line)l" - Hart's quote is an exact substring of it. archive.seattletimes.com/archive/?date=19920103&slug=1468313 redirects to the canonical URL cited.
